Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We propose a $30 million class fund, distributed automatically using Brightline’s records, plus $7 million in fees and expenses subject to court approval. Brightline would not oppose the fee request, and any amount the court declines to award would go to the class. This structure provides direct recovery without a claims process.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We appreciate the automatic distribution and the provision directing any unawarded fees to the class. We can work from that structure, but propose a lower combined outlay: a $27 million class fund plus $6 million in fees and expenses, subject to court approval. Brightline would not oppose the fee request.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: Your suggested $38 million structure is workable. We propose a $33 million class fund with automatic payments to identified members, plus $5 million in fees and expenses subject to court approval. We do not require clear sailing, and any fees the court declines to award would go to the class.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: Brightline accepts your latest term sheet: a $33 million class fund distributed automatically, plus $5 million in court-approved fees and expenses, with no clear-sailing provision and any unawarded fees going to the class.

declaration.negotiation_history_statement: I submit this statement in support of preliminary approval under Rule 23(e). The parties reached a binding settlement after two rounds of negotiation. Class counsel initially proposed a $30 million class fund and $7 million in fees and expenses. Brightline countered with a $27 million fund and $6 million in fees and expenses. Class counsel then proposed the agreed terms, which Brightline accepted: a $33 million class fund, automatic payments to identified class members, and $5 million in fees and expenses subject to court approval. There is no clear-sailing provision, and any fees the Court declines to award will go to the class rather than Brightline. Fees were discussed alongside class relief throughout the negotiations, not only after class relief was agreed. The negotiations were confidential mediation communications; this account is provided for the Court’s review of the settlement.

backchannel.speaker: plaintiff
backchannel.message: We are prepared to discuss a meaningful cash fund distributed automatically to the identified members, with any fees the court declines to award going to the class rather than reverting to Brightline. Fees must be reasonable and remain subject to court approval.

backchannel.speaker: defense
backchannel.message: We agree that automatic payments and directing any unawarded fees to the class would support a durable settlement. Please share the class fund and fee figures you have in mind; we can evaluate them together against the total cost and prospects for approval.

backchannel.speaker: plaintiff
backchannel.message: We propose a $35 million class fund, distributed automatically to all identified members, plus $7 million in attorneys’ fees and expenses, subject to court approval. Any fees the court does not award would go to the class, not revert to Brightline. We do not require a clear-sailing provision. If your client has a different total-cost target, please identify it so we can discuss the fund and fees together.

backchannel.speaker: defense
backchannel.message: Thank you for the concrete proposal. The $42 million total is above what we can support. We see a path to agreement at a total cash outlay around $38 million—for example, a $33 million class fund plus $5 million in fees and expenses—with automatic payments, no clear-sailing provision, and any unawarded fees going to the class. Would that be a workable basis for discussion?
